## Highlights since 0.18.0

- **A native Lattice on Apple silicon Macs, when you want it.** On a Mac with Apple silicon, Lattice can now switch to its native version, drawn by the Mac's graphics hardware instead of a web page. It looks and works the way Lattice does. Switching is your choice: Lattice asks once after this update, and Settings › Editor & builds › Switch to the new Lattice offers it any time. On the first switch your recent projects, settings, themes, plugins, project templates, Agent skills and Overleaf links come with you. The native version has no grammar check and no dictionaries for other languages, and past Agent threads don't show in it. This version's data stays untouched, and changes made in the native version don't flow back; its Settings can switch back to the classic version at any time. Intel Macs, Windows and Linux keep the current Lattice.
- **Spell check in the native Lattice.** The native Lattice checks spelling in .tex, Markdown and text files with macOS's own spell checker, in the language macOS detects for each paragraph, so Chinese prose is never marked. Right-click a marked word for suggestions, Ignore Spelling or Learn Spelling. Words in the project dictionary are left alone, and Settings › Editor & builds › Check spelling turns the check off. Grammar checking and the dictionaries for other languages are not part of the native version.
- **More recent projects.** Lattice now keeps your last 100 projects instead of 8. Below the three cards on the welcome screen, More projects lists the next 20, and Open a recent project… searches all of them by name and folder; the project switcher, File › Open Recent and the command palette open it too. Folders linked to Overleaf are marked, and a folder that has gone missing stays in the list, marked, instead of being dropped.
- **Side panels share one surface.** Project, Papers, the outline and the Agent's page now sit on one surface, a tone below the editor, which follows your theme and light or dark. In the native Lattice, the Agent's page follows named themes such as Nord too.
- **Live preview in the PDF's separate window.** The PDF's separate window now shows the live preview too, updating as you type, just like the PDF beside the editor. This works in the native Lattice as well.
- **Lattice Beta is now Lattice.** If you tried Lattice Beta, you can delete it: the native Lattice is now offered in Lattice itself. Lattice Beta keeps its own data and gets no more updates.
